indication: Refractory or relapsed poor-risk acute myeloid leukemia
design: Multicentre single-arm phase 2 (Polish Adult Leukemia Group), 11 centres
intervention: CLAG-M (cladribine 5 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2, G-CSF)
intervention_dosing: Cladribine 5 mg/m2 + cytarabine 2 g/m2 + mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 with G-CSF; second CLAG-M course for partial response
endpoint: Complete remission (CR) after one or two courses
quality: med (single-arm phase 2, pre-venetoclax era, no post-allo subgroup)
inclusion_match_notes: A true CR rate, not a composite: 66 of 118 reached CR, 49 were refractory and 8 died early. The cohort was poor-risk refractory/relapsed AML, which matches her, but it predates venetoclax entirely and reports no post-allo-HCT subgroup, so the 58% cannot be read across to a patient who has already failed FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax after a transplant. Poor karyotype was the only variable that cut disease-free survival, and WBC above 10 g/L predicted treatment failure.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Single-institution retrospective comparative cohort (Moffitt), CLAG n=97 vs MEC n=65
intervention_dosing: Institutional CLAG and MEC salvage schedules
endpoint: Complete remission (CR) rate, CLAG vs MEC
quality: low-med (retrospective, unadjusted, single centre; ROBINS-I serious confounding risk)
inclusion_match_notes: The only head-to-head remission-induction comparison between two deliverable salvage backbones in this dossier, and it favours the cladribine regimen on true CR (37.9% vs 23.8%, p=0.048). In primary refractory disease the gap widened to 45.5% vs 22.2% but stopped short of significance at n=162. Retrospective allocation means the CLAG advantage could reflect who was chosen for which regimen, and neither arm was analysed for post-allo relapse or venetoclax exposure.
sponsor: H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center and Research Institute

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Single-centre retrospective cohort (Cleveland Clinic), MEC 2014-2022
intervention_dosing: Institutional MEC salvage schedule
endpoint: Overall remission rate (CR + CRi); CR and CRi reported separately
inclusion_match_notes: The CR and CRi components are reported separately here, so the true CR rate is 33.3% of 60 and the 51.7% headline is a composite. The blast-burden gradient is what makes this row bear on her directly: patients starting MEC with marrow blasts at or below 20% and peripheral blasts at or below 30% were more than twice as likely to reach CR/CRi, and she sits at roughly 85% marrow and 82% peripheral. Thirty-five percent of the cohort needed intensive care during the admission.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Multicentre open-label single-arm phase 1/2 (RELAX), German study group
intervention_dosing: Venetoclax 400 mg orally days 1-14 with 3-day ramp-up; mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 days 5-7; cytarabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily days 3-5 at the recommended phase 2 dose
endpoint: Composite complete remission rate (CRc) by intention to treat
quality: med (single-arm phase 2, prospective, multicentre; composite primary endpoint)
inclusion_match_notes: Highest remission figure among the deliverable chemotherapy backbones and the one with the most post-transplant patients: 19 of 55 (35%) had a prior allogeneic HCT. The 75% is explicitly a composite CRc by intention to treat, with no CR-only split published, so it cannot be quoted as a CR rate. Enrolment required relapse from first or second CR or no response after one or two standard inductions, which puts her second-salvage venetoclax-refractory state outside the studied population even though every drug in the regimen is on the shelf.
sponsor: Technische Universität Dresden / German AML study groups (AbbVie funded)

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia, fit for intensive chemotherapy
design: Single-institution phase 1b/2, dose de-escalation then expansion (MD Anderson)
intervention_dosing: CPX-351 at daunorubicin 44 mg/m2 days 1, 3, 5 with venetoclax 300 mg days 2-8 (dose level -2, the RP2D)
endpoint: Overall response rate and composite complete remission rate (CRc)
inclusion_match_notes: Prior venetoclax was allowed and 58% of the cohort had it, 30% had a prior transplant, and 44% were in second salvage or later, which is closer to her position than most salvage series get. The 39% is a composite CRc with no CR-only figure; the 70% CRc headline belongs to the first-salvage TP53-wild-type subgroup, and she is neither. Prior anthracycline exposure and her unresolved TP53 status both cut against the subgroup where the regimen performed.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Phase 1/2 dose-escalation and expansion, uproleselan added to MEC
intervention_dosing: Uproleselan 10 mg/kg twice daily (RP2D) with mitoxantrone, etoposide, cytarabine
endpoint: Remission rate (CR/CRi), with CR reported separately
quality: med for the phase 2 signal, superseded by a negative phase 3
inclusion_match_notes: Reports CR separately from the composite, which is what this question needs: 35% CR and 41% CR/CRi at the recommended dose in 47 R/R patients. The confirmatory phase 3 in R/R AML (NCT03616470) is terminated, so the signal never converted and the agent is not a deliverable option. That phase 3 also excluded secondary refractory AML, the category she now falls into after failing reinduction for her current relapse.

indication: Persistent, relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
biomarker: CD33 expression on at least 20% of blasts by flow or IHC
design: Single-arm phase 2, University of Maryland
intervention: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin)
intervention_dosing: CLAG backbone with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin
endpoint: Response rate (efficacy) and treatment-emergent adverse events
inclusion_match_notes: Written to accept exactly her situation: post-allogeneic-HCT relapse is eligible at 60 days or more from stem-cell infusion provided GVHD is no worse than grade 1 and immunosuppression has been off for two weeks, there is no blast or WBC cap, and prior fludarabine does not trip the exclusion, which names cladribine and gemtuzumab rather than FLAG. Isolated myeloid sarcoma is excluded but she has marrow involvement, so the thigh lesion does not disqualify her; the protocol says nothing about assessing it at response. Two gates remain unverified in her chart: CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, and creatinine below 1.8 mg/dL with direct bilirubin under twice normal.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
biomarker: CD33 positive on more than 25% of blasts by flow cytometry
design: Phase 1 3+3 dose escalation plus RP2D expansion, Medical College of Wisconsin
intervention_dosing: CLAG-M days 1-6, then lintuzumab-Ac225 0.25-1.0 µCi/kg on day 7 (±2); RP2D 0.75 µCi/kg
endpoint: Maximum tolerated dose, RP2D, safety; composite complete remission (CR/CRi) as efficacy
quality: low-med (phase 1, n=26, no CR-only split, single centre)
inclusion_match_notes: Carries the best subgroup numbers on two of her three hardest axes: 50% in TP53-mutated patients and 38.5% in prior-venetoclax patients, against 56.6% overall in 26 patients. Every one of those is a composite CR/CRi with no CR-only split, and the subgroup denominators are single digits to low teens. Prior transplant was explicitly allowed by the protocol, but the study is completed and the follow-on venetoclax combination (NCT06802523) is suspended, so the alpha-emitter is not obtainable on a trial today.
sponsor: Medical College of Wisconsin / Actinium Pharmaceuticals

indication: Acute myeloblastic leukemia in first relapse
design: Prospective single-arm phase 2 (ALFA group, MyloFrance-1)
intervention_dosing: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7, one course
endpoint: Complete remission (CR), with CRp reported separately
inclusion_match_notes: A clean CR figure with the CRp broken out: 15 of 57 reached CR (26%) and 4 more reached CRp (7%). The population is first relapse with no prior transplant and no venetoclax, which makes 26% an upper bound rather than an estimate for refractory post-allo disease. It anchors what single-agent CD33 targeting delivers, and by extension why the CD33 candidates that matter here are the chemotherapy combinations.

indication: Extramedullary myeloid leukemia (CD33-positive), paediatric
design: Case series with serial FDG-PET/CT imaging
intervention_dosing: Not specified per patient
endpoint: Clinical and radiographic response of extramedullary disease
effect_size: Reduction of extramedullary disease on clinical exam and FDG-PET/CT in 2 of 2
inclusion_match_notes: Included because it is the only source found that measured an extramedullary CD33-positive lesion at response rather than assuming the marrow answer covered it. Two paediatric patients, imaged serially by FDG-PET/CT, both with shrinking extramedullary disease on gemtuzumab. Nothing about n=2 supports a response estimate for her thigh sarcoma; it establishes that the assessment is feasible and that a CD33 agent has reached extramedullary sites.
sponsor: Seattle Children's Hospital / Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia, CD123-positive
design: First-in-human phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion; figures are for the RP2D cohort
intervention_dosing: 0.045 mg/kg once every 3 weeks (RP2D)
endpoint: Maximum tolerated dose and RP2D; overall response and composite complete remission as secondary
quality: med for safety, low for the efficacy estimate (n=29 at RP2D)
inclusion_match_notes: Single-agent CD123 targeting reached a 17% composite complete remission rate in 29 patients at the recommended dose, with a 95% CI running from 6% to 36%. Entry required ECOG 0-1, which she meets, but no CR-only figure exists and the confidence interval covers everything from negligible to moderate. Her CD123 positivity is qualitative flow with no antigen density, which is the same gap the source case flagged for every CD123 candidate.

indication: CD123-positive relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
biomarker: CD123 by flow or IHC with no minimum threshold for positivity
design: Single-centre phase 1/2, Stanford
intervention_dosing: Tagraxofusp with low-intensity cladribine/cytarabine; RP2D being determined
endpoint: Recommended phase 2 dose; complete response and composite CR (CR+CRi+CRh) as secondary
inclusion_match_notes: Attractive on the antigen axis and closed on the therapy axis. CD123 needs no minimum threshold, which suits her qualitative-only flow, and the secondary endpoints separate CR from the CR/CRi/CRh composite, which is the reporting discipline this question wants. But eligibility admits only patients whose sole prior therapy was venetoclax plus a hypomethylating agent (with an IDH or FLT3 inhibitor afterwards permitted), and she has had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax and an allograft, so she is excluded outright.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with TP53 abnormalities
design: Post-hoc correlative subgroup of the CP-MGD006-01 flotetuzumab trial
intervention: Flotetuzumab (MGD006), CD123 x CD3 bispecific DART
intervention_dosing: Continuous infusion per CP-MGD006-01 schedule
endpoint: Complete response, defined in this analysis as under 5% marrow blasts
quality: low (post-hoc, n=15, non-ELN response definition, drug discontinued)
inclusion_match_notes: Seven of 15 patients with TP53-abnormal R/R AML responded, which is the strongest TP53-specific remission signal anywhere in this dossier. Two things blunt it: the response definition used here is under 5% marrow blasts rather than ELN CR with count recovery, and the analysis was post-hoc on 15 patients. Flotetuzumab development stopped and NCT02152956 is terminated, so the signal is stranded and cannot be the answer no matter how her TP53 workup resolves.

indication: Relapsed or poor-response acute myeloid leukemia scheduled for allogeneic HSCT
design: Randomised open-label phase 3 non-inferiority (ASAP): remission induction vs watchful waiting into sequential-conditioning allograft
intervention: Immediate allogeneic HSCT after non-intensive disease control (watchful waiting)
comparator: Remission induction with high-dose cytarabine plus mitoxantrone (HAM) before allogeneic HSCT
intervention_dosing: Disease control preferentially watchful waiting; comparator HAM cytarabine 3 g/m2 twice daily days 1-3 (1 g/m2 if over 60 or comorbid) with mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 days 3-5
endpoint: Treatment success, defined as complete remission on day 56 after allogeneic HSCT
quality: high for the randomised comparison (RoB 2 low-some concerns; open label)
inclusion_match_notes: The one randomised test of whether inducing CR before transplant is worth doing, and it found day-56 post-transplant CR of 83% with watchful waiting against 79% with HAM induction. That reframes the question rather than answering it: for a patient going to an allograft, the conditioning produced the remission and the induction added toxicity and 27 more hospital days without adding remissions. She cannot be read into the trial population, because ASAP excluded any history of allogeneic transplantation, capped WBC below 50 GPt/L, and enrolled first relapse or first-induction poor responders rather than second-salvage refractory disease.

indication: High-risk acute myeloid leukemia and MDS, mostly progressive or refractory disease
biomarker: Unfavourable karyotype in 49% of informative patients
design: Prospective single-arm study of sequential chemotherapy, RIC allograft and prophylactic DLI (FLAMSA-RIC)
intervention: FLAMSA sequential conditioning (fludarabine, cytarabine, amsacrine) into RIC allogeneic HCT with prophylactic donor lymphocyte transfusion
intervention_dosing: Fludarabine 30 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, amsacrine 100 mg/m2 for 4 days; 3 days rest; then 4 Gy TBI, ATG and cyclophosphamide 80-120 mg/kg; DLI from day +120
endpoint: Complete remission induced by the sequential regimen
inclusion_match_notes: Reports CR outright rather than a composite: 66 of 75 (88%), and the authors noted that refractory disease and complex cytogenetics did no worse than the better-prognosis subgroups. The remission here is a property of the whole procedure, chemotherapy plus conditioning plus graft, so it is not comparable with a standalone reinduction CR rate and cannot be quoted alongside one. These were overwhelmingly first transplants two decades before venetoclax-era salvage, and the regimen's applicability to a second allograft after a six-year remission is the open question, not the 88%.

indication: Myeloid malignancies at high risk of relapse, including refractory or relapsed AML
design: Phase 1/2 sequential conditioning into allogeneic HCT, Fred Hutch
intervention: Decitabine + FLAG-Ida followed by total-body irradiation and allogeneic HCT (DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC)
intervention_dosing: Decitabine with fludarabine, cytarabine, G-CSF and idarubicin, then TBI-based conditioning and transplant
endpoint: Non-relapse mortality (phase 1); disease-free survival (phase 2)
inclusion_match_notes: The US sequential-conditioning platform that does not shut her out: prior TBI-containing allografts up to 3 Gy are permitted more than six months out, there is no blast cap, and hydroxyurea or up to two cytarabine doses are allowed for hyperleukocytosis before starting. Prior FLAG-Ida triggers PI case-by-case review only for patients who were sensitive to it, defined as an MRD-negative CR lasting a year, so her refractoriness does not itself exclude her. Three gates are undocumented in her chart and each is hard: ECOG 0-1, creatinine clearance above 60 mL/min, and DLCO at or above 70%; the primary endpoints are mortality and disease-free survival, not remission, so no CR figure will come from this protocol.

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML, MDS or CMML
design: Phase 1 sequential chemotherapy into RIC allogeneic HCT, Fred Hutch
intervention: CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida followed by reduced-intensity conditioning and allogeneic HCT
intervention_dosing: CLAG-M or FLAG-Ida cytoreduction, then TBI/fludarabine-cyclophosphamide RIC with matched, mismatched or haploidentical graft
endpoint: Rate of hematopoietic cell transplantation failure and rate of disease progression
inclusion_match_notes: Same sequential logic as NCT06928662 with a cladribine option instead of decitabine, open at the same centre, and admitting patients whose refractoriness is defined by failure of two cycles of 7+3-like chemotherapy, one cycle of high-dose cytarabine, or two cycles of venetoclax combinations, which describes her. The exclusion list turns on infection, CNS disease and donor matching rather than blast burden or prior transplant. Its endpoints are transplant failure and progression, so like the other conditioning platforms it will not generate a CR rate to compare against reinduction.

indication: Active relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia in patients aged 55 and over
design: Randomised phase 3 (SIERRA): 131I-apamistamab conditioning plus allogeneic HCT vs conventional care
intervention: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab) targeted radioimmunoconditioning followed by allogeneic HCT
intervention_dosing: Patient-specific 131I-apamistamab activity by dosimetry, then reduced-intensity conditioning and allograft
endpoint: Durable complete remission lasting at least 180 days
quality: high for the randomised comparison, low applicability to her (RoB 2 low; indirectness serious)
inclusion_match_notes: Randomised proof that radioimmunoconditioning can carry a patient with active disease to an allograft and a durable CR where conventional salvage produced none, at 17.1% versus 0% of 153 patients. The endpoint is a durable CR at 180 days, a stricter bar than the day-of-response CR rates elsewhere in this dossier, so it reads lower than it plays. SIERRA excluded prior allogeneic HCT and enrolled patients 55 and over, so the row carries mechanism evidence for her and no eligibility.

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Phase 2/3 radioimmunotherapy conditioning before allogeneic transplant
intervention: 131I-apamistamab conditioning with fludarabine/cyclophosphamide and allogeneic HCT
intervention_dosing: Dosimetry-guided 131I-apamistamab followed by reduced-intensity conditioning
endpoint: Durable complete remission and overall survival
inclusion_match_notes: The successor protocol to SIERRA and the only active route to targeted radioimmunoconditioning in the US. It carries forward the prior-allogeneic-HCT exclusion, which the source case already established forecloses her, and it has not opened. Kept so the board can see that the mechanism SIERRA validated has an active successor she still cannot enter.

indication: MDS, CMML or secondary AML with marrow blasts above 5% or high-risk genetics
biomarker: Adverse karyotype or unfavourable mutations including TP53 and KMT2A
design: Phase 1/2 sequential conditioning, Heinrich-Heine University Düsseldorf
intervention: Venetoclax added to FLAMSA (fludarabine, amsacrine, cytarabine) plus treosulfan conditioning into allogeneic HCT
intervention_dosing: Venetoclax with FLAMSA sequential conditioning and treosulfan; tacrolimus/MMF prophylaxis
endpoint: Safety: maximal organ toxicity and grade III or worse adverse events within 30 days of transplant
inclusion_match_notes: The modern venetoclax-era version of FLAMSA sequential conditioning, and she is excluded at the front door: enrolment requires patients untreated apart from hydroxyurea or at most two courses of azacitidine or decitabine with or without venetoclax. She has had FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax and a prior allograft. The primary endpoint is 30-day organ toxicity, so even a matched patient would get no remission rate from it.

indication: AML or MDS relapsed after allogeneic HCT
design: Retrospective single-centre cohort (City of Hope), AML n=69 and MDS n=14
intervention_dosing: Azacitidine or decitabine with venetoclax, institutional dosing
endpoint: Complete response or CR with incomplete haematological recovery
inclusion_match_notes: The closest published population to her on the transplant axis: 83 patients relapsing after allograft, 55% with prior venetoclax and 28% of those having already failed a venetoclax regimen, and prior venetoclax failure did not predict worse survival. The 48% is CR or CRi pooled with no CR-only split, and 30-day mortality was 3.6%. Two gaps matter for her: median time to relapse was 7 months against her six years, and a lower-intensity regimen against roughly 85% marrow blasts is a different proposition from the low-burden disease most of this cohort carried.
sponsor: City of Hope National Medical Center

indication: Relapsed or refractory AML after failure of venetoclax-based salvage
design: Retrospective cohort, Vilnius; 28 patients failing venetoclax salvage, 22 receiving further therapy
intervention_dosing: Heterogeneous; includes venetoclax + actinomycin D ± low-dose cytarabine
endpoint: Overall response rate, defined as complete remission plus morphological leukaemia-free state
inclusion_match_notes: The sobering baseline for her specific axis: among 22 heavily pretreated patients who had already failed venetoclax salvage, 23% responded, and that figure pools CR with morphological leukaemia-free state rather than reporting CR alone. Fifty-seven percent of the cohort had a prior allograft and the median was three prior lines, which is close to where she stands. Three of six patients given venetoclax with actinomycin D did reach CR, a small enough denominator that it reads as a hypothesis rather than an option.

indication: AML relapsed after allogeneic HCT
biomarker: Complex karyotype in 6/21; TP53 mutation in 5/21
design: Retrospective single-centre case series (Vanderbilt), 19 evaluable for response
intervention_dosing: Venetoclax with a hypomethylating agent or low-dose cytarabine, off-label
endpoint: Overall response rate, with CR and CRi reported separately
inclusion_match_notes: Breaks the response out properly: 5 CR and 3 CRi among 19 evaluable, so the true CR rate is 5 of 19 and the 42.1% is an ORR. The cohort carries her adverse features, with complex karyotype in 6 and TP53 mutations in 5 of 21, and every patient had relapsed after transplant. Median time from transplant to relapse was 5.7 months and nobody in the series was venetoclax-refractory going in, which is where she differs.

indication: Secondary or therapy-related AML, AML with extramedullary involvement, and myeloid sarcoma
design: Single-arm phase 2, Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai
intervention: VAM regimen (venetoclax-containing combination) in extramedullary and secondary AML
intervention_dosing: Not specified in the registry record
endpoint: Composite complete remission rate
inclusion_match_notes: The only protocol found anywhere in this search that treats extramedullary disease and myeloid sarcoma as an enrolment category rather than an afterthought, with a composite complete remission primary endpoint. She cannot enter it: enrolment is restricted to previously untreated AML, the age ceiling is 65, and the site is Shanghai. Its existence is the answer to whether anyone is measuring remission in myeloid sarcoma prospectively, and the answer is one recruiting single-centre study in a front-line population.
sponsor: Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

indication: Myeloid sarcoma, de novo and AML-related including secondary AML
design: Multicentre retrospective survey, 9 Italian centres; 43 of 48 treated intensively
intervention: Intensive chemotherapy programmes (FLAI, HDAC-IDA, HyperCVAD, MEC) with allogeneic HCT where feasible
intervention_dosing: Centre-specific intensive schedules
endpoint: Complete remission rate with intensive chemotherapy
inclusion_match_notes: The largest adult myeloid sarcoma series with a remission figure attached: 45% CR across 43 intensively treated patients, with a 5% early death rate. Fifteen of the 48 were secondary-AML-related myeloid sarcoma, the category her thigh lesion falls into, and that subgroup did worse on survival. The paper reports CR for the disease as a whole and does not separate marrow from extramedullary response, so it still does not establish whether a sarcoma clears when the marrow does.
sponsor: Italian multicentre myeloid sarcoma registry (Udine coordinating)

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia
design: Single-arm phase 2, H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center
intervention_dosing: CLAG-M with venetoclax
endpoint: MRD-negative remission rate
inclusion_match_notes: Recruiting, US, and the right regimen class, but she trips four separate exclusions: venetoclax-refractory disease, prior high-dose-cytarabine-containing therapy which names FLAG explicitly, any known history of TP53 mutation, and a WBC ceiling of 25,000. Extramedullary AML with concurrent marrow involvement is allowed, which is the one axis she clears. Logged so the record shows the venetoclax-CLAG-M combinations were checked rather than assumed open.
sponsor: H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center and Research Institute

indication: Acute myeloid leukemia and high-grade myeloid neoplasms
biomarker: ELN adverse risk for the newly diagnosed strata
design: Phase 1/2, University of Washington; R/R patients admitted to the phase 1 portion only
intervention_dosing: CLAG-M with escalating venetoclax; phase 1 established the MTD
endpoint: Adverse events and MTD (phase 1); event-free survival (phase 2)
inclusion_match_notes: Notable for naming extramedullary myeloid sarcoma as a qualifying disease manifestation for relapsed patients, alongside detectable peripheral blasts or 5% marrow blasts. Relapsed and refractory patients were admitted only to the phase 1 portion, and the phase 2 that continues to recruit takes newly diagnosed adverse-risk disease, so the door she would need is the one that has closed. Her venetoclax refractoriness would also work against a venetoclax-containing reinduction on any protocol.
sponsor: University of Washington / Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center

indication: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia, first or second relapse or refractory
design: Randomised pragmatic phase 3 (IMPACT-AML), high-intensity vs low-intensity therapy
intervention_dosing: Pragmatic; local practice regimens in both arms
endpoint: Event-free survival (remission rates collected as secondary)
inclusion_match_notes: The only randomised trial recruiting that would put intensive and non-intensive remission induction against each other in R/R AML, which is the comparison this question lacks. Entry needs the treating physician to consider both arms reasonable and no protocol to be better suited, a judgement that would be hard to defend for a patient with 85% blasts after an allograft. It is Italian, its primary endpoint is event-free survival rather than CR, and nothing has reported.
sponsor: Istituto Romagnolo per lo Studio dei Tumori Dino Amadori IRST IRCCS
